title: Trump Attacks Gold Star Khan Family After DNC Speech
description_short: Trump Attacks Gold Star Khan Family After DNC Speech
description_medium: After Khizr Khan criticized him at the Democratic National Convention, Trump attacked the Gold Star father and suggested his wife was not “allowed to speak.” The public dispute with a family whose son was killed in Iraq drew bipartisan condemnation. The episode became a defining moment in the 2016 campaign for its cruelty and divisiveness.
description_long: At the 2016 Democratic National Convention, Khizr Khan criticized Trump’s proposed restrictions on Muslims and asked whether Trump had read the Constitution. Khan spoke as the father of Army Captain Humayun Khan, who was killed in Iraq in 2004. Trump responded in interviews by questioning the parents and suggesting that Ghazala Khan had been prevented from speaking. The remarks drew criticism from political figures across parties and became one of the campaign’s most widely discussed exchanges. The episode concerned a bereaved military family who had publicly challenged a candidate’s policy and judgment. It did not involve an official government action, but it shaped debate about respect for service members, Muslim Americans, and the limits of campaign rhetoric. The linked CBS and PBS reports document the exchange and public response. This account describes the public statements and the family’s loss without inferring a private motive or adding claims beyond the reporting.

title: Trump-Era Epstein Release Omitted Three FBI 302 Reports Reviewed by The Guardian
description_short: Trump-Era Epstein Release Omitted Three FBI 302 Reports Reviewed by The Guardian
description_medium: The Guardian reported obtaining three missing FBI form-302 reports summarizing interviews that were not included in DOJ's public Epstein-file release. The omission became a transparency flashpoint because these were not random artifacts but core interview records tied to high-profile allegations. Even without proving allegations, withholding central interview documents undermines confidence that disclosure standards were applied consistently.
description_long: The Guardian reported on February 26, 2026, that it had obtained three FBI form-302 memos describing four interviews conducted in 2019. The Department of Justice had not included those memos when it released millions of Epstein-related pages beginning in December. The records contained explicit but unsubstantiated allegations that Trump sexually abused a woman when she was a minor, with Jeffrey Epstein’s assistance. The Guardian said the allegation had not been verified, that the FBI brought no charges based on it, and that some details appeared to conflict with what is known about Epstein’s life at the time. The omission raised questions about whether the public release was complete, while DOJ said withheld material was duplicative or privileged. This is a dispute about disclosure and the handling of records, not proof that the allegation occurred or that officials removed documents for a particular political reason. The account retains the report’s caveats and separates the existence of interview records from the truth of their contents.

This account presents the Guardian’s causal analysis rather than proof that U.S. policy alone caused each British project’s delay. description_short: Trump orders drone strike that kills Iranian General Qasem Soleimani
description_medium: On January 3, 2020, the United States killed Iranian General Qasem Soleimani in a drone strike near Baghdad airport on orders from President Trump. Trump ordered the operation. Soleimani’s killing sharply escalated the confrontation between Washington and Tehran and raised concern about retaliation and a wider regional conflict. The event occurred on Iraqi territory, adding a sovereignty issue to the debate about U.S. military action. The supplied source records the strike and public controversy but does not resolve the competing legal arguments or establish that a broader war was inevitable. This account separates the confirmed operation and its immediate strategic context from claims about the administration’s justification. A judge compelled Pentagon leaders to admit that stated performance justifications for 5400 probationary employee firings were false.

title: Matt Gaetz Nominated as Attorney General
description_short: Matt Gaetz Nominated as Attorney General
description_medium: In November 2024, Trump nominated Matt Gaetz to serve as Attorney General, a shocking selection that sent shockwaves through Washington. Gaetz had recently been the subject of a DOJ investigation into sex trafficking allegations involving a minor. The nomination was widely seen as Trump choosing a loyalist willing to weaponize the Justice Department against his political enemies.
description_long: President-elect Donald Trump announced on November 13, 2024, that he would nominate Representative Matt Gaetz to be attorney general. The appointment would have put a combative Florida Republican in charge of the Justice Department, an agency with authority over federal law enforcement and prosecutions. NPR reported that the choice surprised some senators and that confirmation was uncertain. Gaetz had recently been investigated by the Justice Department over allegations involving sex trafficking of a minor; federal prosecutors ultimately did not bring charges, according to the report. A nomination is not an appointment: the Senate must confirm an attorney general, and the nominee must complete the confirmation process. The existing summary characterizes the selection as a loyalty choice and a risk to DOJ independence, but those are interpretations rather than a finding about what Gaetz would have done. This entry records the nomination, the scrutiny surrounding it, and the distinction between allegations, prosecutorial decisions, and Senate confirmation.
